title: Prelude in C minor, BWV 999
composer: J. S. Bach (Kleines Praludium / lute, BWV 999)
readiness: score-file pending: BWV 999 is NOT in the music21 corpus, so this analysis is curated from analytical knowledge of the piece and has NOT yet been verified against an imported MusicXML/MXL. Drop a 'bwv999_prelude_c_minor.mxl' (or .musicxml) into data/scores/ to enable live rendering; the importer will then fill the literal note content. The annotation contract, the diatonic C-minor mapping, and the honest chromatic marking are fully exercised by this opening excerpt.
global_summary: Bach's C-minor Prelude (BWV 999) is a chromatic arpeggio study. Even its opening bars lean on the harmonic-minor dominant (G major, with a raised leading-tone B-natural), a Neapolitan (Db major), and applied/secondary dominants -- all of which lie OUTSIDE the pilot's diatonic, natural-minor, triad-only engine. Those bars are deliberately marked status='unsupported_chromatic' with an explanation naming the layer they need (harmonic-minor / secondary-dominant / Neapolitan). The genuinely diatonic C-minor bars (i, iv, III, VI, VII, v, ii0) are analysed and mapped to the Atlas and Harmonic Network in full. This is the roadmap signal: BWV 999 motivates a future harmonic-minor + secondary-dominant layer.

sections.label: Opening tonic and dominant
sections.description: Tonic established and answered by the harmonic-minor dominant.

sections.label: Diatonic descent
sections.description: A descent through the natural-minor diatonic triads iv - VII - III - VI - ii0.

sections.label: Chromatic intensification
sections.description: A secondary dominant and a Neapolitan drive toward a half cadence on the dominant -- the chromatic heart of the prelude.

cadences.explanation: Phrygian/Neapolitan approach to a half cadence on the dominant (G major). Both members need the chromatic layer; marked accordingly.

slices.explanation: Dominant of C minor as a MAJOR triad (G-B-D) -- the leading tone B-natural is raised from the natural-minor Bb. Requires the reserved harmonic-minor layer; mapped to the G7 network node by pitch class.
Subdominant (iv, F minor) -- diatonic predominant in natural minor.
Subtonic (VII, Bb major) -- the natural-minor flat-seventh, a diatonic major triad (NOT a leading-tone chord).
Mediant (III, Eb major) -- the relative major triad, a tonic-area colour.
Submediant (VI, Ab major) -- diatonic in natural minor.
Supertonic diminished (ii0, D-F-Ab) -- the diatonic minor-key predominant.
Secondary dominant V7/iv (C7, with chromatic E-natural and Bb) tonicising the subdominant. Reserved secondary-dominant layer; mapped to the C7 network node.
Neapolitan sixth (bII6, Db major) -- a chromatic predominant built on the lowered second degree. Requires the reserved Neapolitan/chromatic layer.
Half cadence on the harmonic-minor dominant (G major, raised leading-tone B). Chromatic; reserved harmonic-minor layer.
